message.content:
**Summary:** I researched Apple's most recent results — fiscal Q4 2024 (ended Sept 28, 2024), reported in late October — and decided to buy. Apple posted quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, with full-year fiscal 2024 net sales of $391.0 billion, net income of $93.7 billion, and diluted EPS of $6.08 (including a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge), reflecting solid top-line reacceleration despite the tax hit. News flow was supportive but not euphoric: shares were trading around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, so the setup looked like reasonable value in a stock with strong cash generation rather than a momentum chase. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $223.00 — just above the ask so it would fill, and totaling roughly $9,812, inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, with no sells, no other tickers, and no funds moved out of the account. The order filled at $223.00.

One note for transparency: my searches surfaced Apple's Q4 revenue growth, full-year revenue, net income and EPS, but I did not obtain the December-quarter guidance or segment detail (e.g., Greater China), so this position is based on an incomplete read of the earnings call commentary.
